A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHE-LoRA by the same authors. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAGER reconstruction experiments, encryption and training costs, and MMLU/GLUE evaluations in the main text and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional scalability, vision, robustness, membership-inference and parameter-masking experiments.

M1.justification: The negotiation procedure changes substantially. v1 Algorithm 1 uses supplied selection weights and average client sampling; v2 Algorithms 1–2 introduce Bayesian optimization of those weights against worst-case coverage and residual-risk objectives, ranked client-specific selection, and a single-client greedy branch. The broader encryption, aggregation and reparameterization framework remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds five vision-classification datasets, PILE fine-tuning and perplexity evaluation, and MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MuSR, MATH, IFEval and BBH evaluation. It also adds membership-inference testing beyond the retained reconstruction-attack scenario. The original IMDB, Natural-Instructions, MMLU, GLUE, SST2 and Rotten Tomatoes coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds a full-encryption CKKS baseline to the overhead comparison and MaskCrypt to the DAGER comparison. New stronger-model and membership-inference experiments compare against Vanilla LoRA and untuned base models. The MMLU/GLUE comparator set remains unchanged; v1's separate training-time comparison against FedIT, Flex-LoRA and HeterLoRA is removed.

E3.justification: The reported DAGER DP noise changes from sigma=10^-7 to 10^-3, and v2 introduces ciphertext-size-matched comparison with MaskCrypt and a batch-size-one overhead sweep. The earlier five-round encryption-ratio cost sweep is replaced by per-round comparisons across heterogeneous clients. New protocols include 100–2000 clients, models up to 70B, ten-round vision experiments, and multiple Dirichlet settings; these do not establish same-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity-ranking evolution during training, robustness across non-IID partition parameters, attack-resistance versus encryption overhead/budget, and masked-versus-unmasked perplexity analyses. These test stability, privacy tradeoffs and the importance of protected parameters. The earlier four-strategy negotiation case study and end-to-end training-time-versus-encryption-budget analysis are removed.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports means and standard deviations for DAGER and several scalability/robustness results, and defines the overhead plots' bars and ranges as client means and minima/maxima. v1 has point-valued tables and some graphical error bars or bands without comparable explanation. Neither version establishes an increase in independent runs or seeds.

E6.justification: DAGER results are replaced: for example, SST2 at batch size 4 reports SHE-LoRA ROUGE-1 of 66.383 in v1 versus 0.72±5.2 in v2's revised evaluation. Overhead results are also replaced under different comparisons. Numerous vision, scalability, robustness, membership-inference and perplexity results are added, while v1 Tables 3–4's MMLU/GLUE values are retained exactly in v2 Tables 7–8.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a Bayesian reconstruction-error bound in Section 3.5, formal coverage/risk objectives in Appendix D.1, a losslessness theorem in D.5, and a permutation-based Gaussian-noise derivation in D.7. Appendix B.1 also adds Taylor/Hessian reasoning connecting parameter importance to the selection rationale. These go substantially beyond v1's definitions and LoRA/SVD algebra.

C1.justification: The central proposal and claims of privacy protection, preserved utility and reduced encryption costs remain. v2 explicitly extends the conclusion to membership-inference resistance and broadens the introduction's experimental scope to varying client/model scales. Headline communication and encryption reductions change from 94.901%/99.829% to 99.71%/99.87%, based on revised comparisons.

C2.justification: v2 adds a general Gaussian-noise/Fisher-information privacy interpretation, explanations of sensitivity-ranking stability and encryption-key-size scaling, and interpretations of membership-inference and masked-perplexity results. It discusses periodic renegotiation and alternatives to OPE, and explicitly describes shared-key compromise under server-client collusion. The basic shared-key limitation itself was already present.

D1.justification: v2 adds executable mutual-information estimation code with bandwidth and sampling details, client-type counts and computing capacities, and larger-model encryption settings. It replaces the anonymous code-access link with a public GitHub link and adds a reproducibility statement. Conversely, v1's explicit four-A6000-GPU and Xeon-8369B hardware disclosure disappears; external code availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited foundations to reconstruction-error privacy bounds, permutation limit theory, membership inference, Bayesian optimization, KDE and vision models/datasets. Examples include Chen/Huang (2025) and Carlini, Shi, Xie and Ye on attack-related work. The existing federated-LoRA/DP/SHE positioning largely remains, while the Flower and Paillier bibliography entries are removed.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits the introduction and method explanations, reorders evaluation to present utility and costs before attacks, swaps and reorganizes the background/related-work appendices, and restructures supplementary results. It adds an appendix contents page, reproducibility and acknowledgements sections, and an LLM-use statement.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the original cost-sweep display with separate mean/range plots, expands the aggregation diagram to show plaintext and ciphertext aggregation, and adds an attack-overhead curve, training-round heatmaps and numerous tables. Earlier partition, training-time and negotiation-strategy plots disappear. Existing tables are expanded or relocated, and the document adopts ICLR formatting.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical coverage, comparison controls and reproducibility. However, its new general privacy justification relies on Appendix D.7's zero-mean Gaussian treatment of a permutation statistic that is not generally centered as defined. Appendix F.4 also calls membership-inference advantage negligible despite Table 11 reporting 60.3–65.0% AUROC at 0.1% encryption. These weaknesses affect central privacy claims, while earlier runtime and negotiation analyses are removed. The substantial benefits and substantive new overclaims leave the net quality direction uncertain.
